title: API Changeset
description: A structured specification for communicating API mutations between two versions of an OpenAPI document. A changeset document describes 'how we got from spec A to spec B' in a form that is both human-readable and machine-parseable. Operations fall into four families: structural (shape), constraint (rules), semantic (meaning), and lifecycle (status). Operations in the semantic family (resemanticize, retime, reorder) and documentation-only operations (annotate) are author-only: a spec-diff tool cannot detect them by comparing two OpenAPI documents, which is the primary reason this format exists alongside the specs rather than being derived from them.

changeset_version.description: Version of the changeset schema format itself (this spec), in semver.

api.description: Identifies which API and which pair of versions this changeset describes.

released.description: Date the 'to' version was released to consumers.

summary.description: Brief human-readable overview of this changeset.

notices.description: Changeset-level announcements not tied to a specific change entry (e.g., urgent security guidance).

changes.description: The list of individual changes that together constitute this changeset. Per-file changesets are encouraged for git workflows (one changeset per release, or one per-change file aggregated at build time); aggregated changesets are better for consumption. The schema supports both — consumers should be liberal in what they accept.

spec_reference.description: Identifies a specific OpenAPI document by version and (optionally) location.

version.description: API version identifier (semver, date, or opaque string).

spec.description: URL or relative path to the OpenAPI document.

spec_hash.description: Optional content hash (e.g. sha256:...) for integrity verification.

operation.description: The kind of mutation. Operations are grouped into four families: structural (shape), constraint (rules), semantic (meaning), and lifecycle (status). Semantic-family ops plus 'annotate' are author-only and cannot be recovered from a spec diff — tooling should treat their absence from a diff as non-evidence, not as validation failure.

oneOf.description: Structural. A new element was introduced. Requires 'to'.
Structural. An element was deleted. Requires 'from'.
Structural. Same element, new identifier. Requires 'from' and 'to'.
Structural. Same element, new location (e.g., flattened or nested). Requires 'from' and 'to'.
Structural. One element became many. Requires 'from' (single) and 'to' (array).
Structural. Many elements became one. Requires 'from' (array) and 'to' (single).
Structural. Element swapped for a different one with similar intent. Requires 'from' and 'to'.
Structural. Schema composition reshuffled (allOf/oneOf/anyOf restructured without semantic change). Requires 'from' and 'to'.
Constraint. Validation rules became stricter (required added, narrower type, smaller max, etc.). Requires 'at'.
Constraint. Validation rules became more permissive. Requires 'at'.
Constraint. Rules changed in a way that is neither strictly stricter nor strictly looser (e.g., swapped format from email to URI). Requires 'at'.
Constraint. Type changed (e.g., string→int, int32→int64, scalar→object). Requires 'at'.
Constraint. Default value changed. Requires 'at'.
Constraint. Encoding/format/units changed (ISO date→unix, dollars→cents, etc.). Requires 'at'.
Semantic (author-only). Same shape, different meaning. Cannot be detected by spec diff. Requires 'at'.
Semantic (author-only). Ordering semantics changed. Requires 'at'.
Semantic (author-only). Timing/consistency semantics changed (sync→eventual, immediate→batched). Requires 'at'.
Semantic (author-only). Documentation-only clarification with no wire-format change. Requires 'at'.
Lifecycle. Element still works but is scheduled for removal. Requires 'at' and 'lifecycle'.
Lifecycle. Removal date committed. Requires 'at' and 'lifecycle.sunset_date'.
Lifecycle. Element un-deprecated. Requires 'at'.
Lifecycle. Element removed before previously-announced sunset (emergency). Requires 'from'.

target_kind.description: What kind of thing the operation applies to. Orthogonal to the operation itself.

json_pointer.description: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into the referenced OpenAPI document. May be prefixed with '#' for URI-fragment style.

pointer_or_pointers.description: A single JSON Pointer OR an array of JSON Pointers. An array signals that one logical change applies to multiple coordinated locations (e.g., renaming a field that appears in 12 endpoint schemas is ONE change entry with a 12-element pointer array, not 12 linked entries).

cross_reference.description: A reference to another change entry. May be a bare ID (same changeset) or an object scoping to a different changeset document by version and change ID.

oneOf.description: Change ID within the same changeset document.

changeset.description: Version identifier of the other changeset document (e.g., '2.3.0').

url.description: Optional direct URL to the referenced changeset document.

id.description: Stable identifier for this change (e.g., 'CHG-001'). Used for cross-referencing.

from.description: Pointer(s) into the 'from' OpenAPI spec. Required for ops that remove or transform an existing element. An array means the single logical change is mirrored at N coordinated locations.

to.description: Pointer(s) into the 'to' OpenAPI spec. Required for ops that add or transform into new location. An array means the single logical change is mirrored at N coordinated locations.

at.description: Pointer into both specs, for ops that modify an element in place (e.g., deprecate, retype).

breaking.description: Shorthand: true iff this change requires consumer-side modification to keep working. Equivalent to 'severity == breaking'. Retained for authoring ergonomics; 'severity' is the authoritative field if both are set.

severity.description: Attention level for consumers. 'info' = cosmetic or internal, 'notice' = non-breaking but behavior-affecting (new enum values, new required response fields that affect log storage, new rate limits), 'breaking' = consumer must act. Non-breaking changes can still warrant attention — this axis is strictly richer than the 'breaking' boolean.

detectable.description: Whether a spec-diff tool can surface this change by comparing the two OpenAPI documents. Defaults TRUE for structural/constraint/lifecycle ops, FALSE for semantic-family ops (resemanticize, reorder, retime) and 'annotate'. Authors may override when a structural change happens to be diff-invisible (e.g., a retype where the new type renders identically). Validators use this field to decide whether a missing diff entry is suspicious.

rationale.description: Why this change is being made.

before.description: Optional inline snapshot of the relevant spec fragment before the change.

after.description: Optional inline snapshot of the relevant spec fragment after the change.

related.description: Cross-references to logically related changes (same or other changeset documents).

supersedes.description: Cross-references to prior changes this one supersedes or reverses. Use the object form with 'changeset' when pointing to a different changeset document.

migration.description: Guidance for consumers on how to handle this change.

server_behavior.description: What the server does during the transition window.

dual_support.description: Window during which both old and new behaviors coexist.

automated.description: True if an SDK / codegen / gateway can absorb the change with no consumer code changes.

lifecycle.description: Lifecycle transition metadata, aligned with RFC 9745 (Deprecation) and RFC 8594 (Sunset).

sunset_date.description: Must be >= deprecated_date (validated by tooling, not by schema).

replacement.description: JSON Pointer to the recommended alternative element.
